title: Chirality destroys oriented active solids
authors: S. J. Kole, Gareth P. Alexander, Ananyo Maitra, Sriram Ramaswamy
abstract: We construct a hydrodynamic theory of the effect of chiral and active force densities on three-dimensional uniaxial solids. We show that in a fixed background medium active chiral force densities---that arise at lower order in gradients than odd elasticity---generically destabilise the solid state. We further show this active instability also affects isotropic chiral solids in an anisotropic medium, a situation that is relevant for cell clusters moving through the extracellular matrix. Interestingly, the instability is eliminated in a higher-symmetry solid, known as the polar elastomer; indeed, we show that chirality does not affect the leading-order mechanics of such materials. We further demonstrate that momentum-conserving polar active solids have two chiral odd elasticities in contrast to the one discussed for two-dimensional solids. However, we again find that the higher symmetry of polar elastomers eliminates one of these with the remaining one being equivalent to the two-dimensional odd elastic force density. Our results should apply to numerous biological and condensed matter systems.
summary: This theoretical work develops a hydrodynamic theory to examine how chirality and active forces destabilize solid materials. It demonstrates that while these forces generally cause instability, the enhanced symmetry of polar elastomers allows them to remain stable. The findings are highly relevant for understanding biological tissues and active matter systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates how chiral and active force densities affect the stability of three-dimensional uniaxial solids.
main_result: Active chiral force densities generically destabilize the solid state, but this instability is eliminated in higher-symmetry materials like polar elastomers.
method: The authors construct and analyze a hydrodynamic theory, using linearized equations and wavevector perturbations to study the dynamics.
model_or_system: The study models 3D uniaxial solids and polar elastomers using continuum mechanics, incorporating free energy functionals and active force tensors.
key_observables: Instability growth rate, helical transverse displacement field, and the comparison of odd elastic force densities.
important_parameters: Chiral and active force densities, wavevector magnitude (q), and elastic moduli ($\lambda, \mu, r, w, t, s$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a vacancy-free solid and compares general uniaxial solids to the higher symmetry of elastomers.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the considered oriented solids and the generic helical instability.
paper_structure: The paper develops a hydrodynamic theory, analyzes the instability in general uniaxial solids, and then contrasts these findings with the stability observed in higher-symmetry polar elastomers.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter mechanics, the study of active instabilities and symmetry breaking in non-equilibrium systems has parallels with understanding dissipation and steady states in complex quantum or many-body systems.
